CJP's philosophy explicitly rejects any framework that prioritizes one over the other -- economic development is not an excuse to sacrifice civil liberties; civil liberties are not an excuse to ignore economic development.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered February 7, 2007 as the keynote at the 9th National Ayala Young Leaders Congress -- invited by Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala; Ayala Corporation has run AYLC since 1998 as its 'strategic investment on the youth' -- this address by CJP is the most comprehensive post-retirement statement of his vision-mission framework. He opens with a striking personal admission: 'I was very poor and orphaned early in life. I had nothing. No worldly treasures to keep, no reputation to protect, no close relatives to defer to' -- the absence of protection-worthy stakes as the source of his independence and reformist drive. He founded NUSP 'as a rebellion against a decadent student milieu... founded on the proposition that the best in a person and in society can be attained only in freedom, dignity, equality and shared responsibility.' He presents the Chief Justice's dual role (primus inter pares + leader of the judicial branch) and his full vision-mission: vision (judiciary safeguarding liberty and nurturing prosperity under the rule of law); four missions for three constituencies -- (1) four Ins (independence, integrity, industry, intelligence) for 15 justices and 2,000 judges; (2) ACID problems (access, corruption, incompetence, delay) to overcome; (3) EC (ethics and competence) to revitalize the legal profession; (4) DHL (dedication, honesty, loyalty) for 26,000 judicial employees. Three landmark Panganiban Court decisions (Senate v. Ermita, Bayan v. Ermita, David v. Arroyo) exemplify liberty safeguarding; Tanada and La Bugal exemplify deferential interpretation for prosperity. Rule of law: 'My Vision is not liberty or prosperity; it is liberty and prosperity. These twin beacons of justice must go together... freedom and food, democracy and development, ethics and economics, integrity and investments.' He closes with the MVP/PLDT three-day story (fourth telling: 60 cars kept one; briefcase cash deposited; arrived at 8 AM without comment; result: PLDT's worth multiplied tenfold and corporate ethics a hundredfold). 'Visionary leadership by example.'
